subject: Government
examFormat: Two compulsory papers taken as a composite at one sitting. Paper 1: fifty multiple-choice questions drawn from the entire syllabus, all answered in 1 hour for 40 marks. Paper 2: a 2-hour essay test for 60 marks in two sections: Section A (Elements of Government) has five questions of which two are attempted; Section B (Political and Constitutional Developments in West Africa and International Relations) has a set of five questions per member country, of which two are answered from the candidate's own country.
excluded: Section B items specific to Ghana, Sierra Leone, The Gambia and Liberia (pre-colonial systems, constitutions, political parties, military rule, federal/unitary systems and foreign policies of those countries), because only the Nigeria items apply.

topics.name: Meaning and Scope of Government
topics.content: Government as an institution of the state (definition of state, features, structure and functions); government as a process or art of governing; government as an academic field of study and the reasons for studying government.

subtopics.name: Government as an Institution of the State
objectives: Define the state and state its features, structure and functions

subtopics.name: Government as a Process or Art of Governing
objectives: Explain government as a process or art of governing

subtopics.name: Government as an Academic Field of Study
objectives: Give reasons for studying government

topics.name: Basic Concepts of Government
objectives: Explain the meaning and features of the basic concepts of government
topics.content: Meaning and features of: state, society, nation, power, authority, legitimacy, sovereignty, democracy, political culture and socialization, communalism, feudalism and oligarchy, liberalism, socialism, communism, capitalism, fascism, aristocracy and totalitarianism.

topics.name: Basic Principles of Government
objectives: Explain the basic principles of government
topics.content: Rule of law; fundamental human rights; separation of powers/checks and balances; constitutionalism; political participation; representative government; centralization and decentralization (delegated legislation, devolution and decentralization).

topics.name: Constitutions
topics.content: Definition and sources of constitutions; functions; types and features (written and unwritten, rigid and flexible).

subtopics.name: Definition and Sources of Constitutions
objectives: Define a constitution and identify its sources

subtopics.name: Functions of Constitutions
objectives: State the functions of a constitution

subtopics.name: Types and Features of Constitutions
objectives: Distinguish written from unwritten and rigid from flexible constitutions, and state their features

topics.name: Organs of Government
objectives: Describe the types, structure, composition/membership, functions, powers and limitations of the Executive, the Legislature and the Judiciary
Explain judicial independence
topics.content: The Executive, the Legislature and the Judiciary, with judicial independence: types, structure, composition/membership, functions, powers and limitations.

topics.name: State Structure and Characteristics of Government
objectives: Explain the meaning, types, features, merits and demerits of each type of state structure and form of government
topics.content: Types: unitary, federal, confederal, presidential or non-parliamentary, parliamentary or cabinet, monarchical and republican. Meaning, types, features, merits and demerits.

topics.name: Citizenship
objectives: Explain the meaning of citizenship and the modes of its acquisition
State the rights, duties and obligations of individuals in the state
Identify means of safeguarding the rights of citizens

topics.name: Political Parties and Party Systems
topics.content: Political parties: definition, organization/structure and functions. Party systems: definition, types, merits and demerits.

subtopics.name: Political Parties
objectives: Define political parties and describe their organization/structure and functions

subtopics.name: Party Systems
objectives: Define party systems and describe their types, merits and demerits

topics.name: Pressure Groups, Public Opinion and Mass Media
topics.content: Pressure groups: definition, types, mode of operation and functions. Public opinion: definition, formation, measurement and importance. Mass media: definition, roles and impact.

subtopics.name: Pressure Groups
objectives: Define pressure groups and describe their types, mode of operation and functions

subtopics.name: Public Opinion
objectives: Define public opinion and explain its formation, measurement and importance

subtopics.name: Mass Media
objectives: Define the mass media and describe their roles and impact

topics.name: Electoral Systems, Processes and Electoral Management Body
topics.content: Electoral systems and processes: meaning and purpose of elections; franchise (meaning and limitations); types, advantages and disadvantages of electoral systems. Electoral management body: definition, function, problems/constraints.

subtopics.name: Electoral Systems and Processes
objectives: Explain the meaning and purpose of elections
Explain franchise and its limitations
Describe the types, advantages and disadvantages of electoral systems

subtopics.name: Electoral Management Body
objectives: Define an electoral management body and describe its functions and problems/constraints

topics.name: Public/Civil Service Administration
topics.content: Public/civil service: meaning, structure, characteristics and functions. Public/Civil Service Commission: meaning and functions. Public corporations: definition, purposes, functions, control, challenges, need for commercialization and privatization. Local governments: meaning, structure, purposes, functions, sources of revenue, control and problems.

subtopics.name: Public/Civil Service
objectives: Explain the meaning, structure, characteristics and functions of the public/civil service

subtopics.name: Public/Civil Service Commission
objectives: Explain the meaning and functions of the Public/Civil Service Commission

subtopics.name: Public Corporations
objectives: Define public corporations and describe their purposes, functions, control and challenges
Explain the need for commercialization and privatization

subtopics.name: Local Governments
objectives: Explain the meaning, structure, purposes and functions of local governments
Identify the sources of revenue, control and problems of local governments

topics.name: Pre-Colonial Political System of Nigeria
objectives: Describe the structural organization of the Hausa/Fulani, Yoruba and Igbo political systems
topics.content: The structural organization of the Hausa/Fulani, the Yoruba and the Igbo.

topics.name: Colonial Administration
topics.content: The policy and structure of British colonial administration (Crown Colony, Protectorate and Indirect Rule); the policy of French colonial administration (Assimilation and Association, Loi Cadre); impact, advantages and disadvantages of colonial rule.

subtopics.name: British Colonial Administration
objectives: Explain the policy and structure of British colonial administration: Crown Colony, Protectorate and Indirect Rule

subtopics.name: French Colonial Administration
objectives: Explain the French colonial policies of Assimilation and Association (Loi Cadre)

subtopics.name: Impact of Colonial Rule
objectives: Assess the impact, advantages and disadvantages of colonial rule

topics.name: Nationalism in Nigeria
objectives: Explain the meaning, factors and effects of nationalism
Identify the key nationalist leaders/movements and their contributions

topics.name: Constitutional Developments in Nigeria
topics.content: Pre-independence constitutions (features): Clifford 1922, Richards 1946, Macpherson 1951 and Littleton 1954. Post-independence constitutions (features): Independence Constitution 1960, Republican Constitution 1963, the 1979 and 1989 Constitutions, and the 1999 Constitution (origin, features, strengths and weaknesses).

subtopics.name: Pre-Independence Constitutions of Nigeria
objectives: Describe the features of the Clifford 1922, Richards 1946, Macpherson 1951 and Littleton 1954 constitutions

subtopics.name: Post-Independence Constitutions of Nigeria
objectives: Describe the features of the Independence Constitution 1960, Republican Constitution 1963 and the 1979 and 1989 Constitutions
Describe the origin, features, strengths and weaknesses of the 1999 Constitution

topics.name: Development of Major Political Parties in Nigeria
objectives: Describe the formation, objectives, sources of finance, achievements and failures of the major political parties in Nigeria

topics.name: Military Rule in Nigeria
objectives: Explain the causes and effects of military rule in Nigeria
Identify the various military regimes

topics.name: Federal System of Government in Nigeria
objectives: Describe the origin, factors, structure, features and problems of the federal system in Nigeria

topics.name: Foreign Policy of Nigeria
objectives: Define foreign policy and explain the factors, objectives, advantages and disadvantages of Nigeria's foreign policy

topics.name: International Organizations
objectives: Describe the origin, aims/objectives, achievements and problems of the United Nations Organization (UNO), the Commonwealth of Nations, the African Union (AU)/NEPAD and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
topics.content: The United Nations Organization (UNO); the Commonwealth of Nations; the African Union (AU) - NEPAD; the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). Origin, aims/objectives, achievements and problems.
